chunks: Three (things) complain to God, Mighty and Majestic: a ruined mosque whose people do not pray in it, a scholar among ignorant ones, and a mushaf (Quran) hanging (somewhere), dust having settled upon it, not being recited from.

key_terms.الْغُبَارُ: Dust — a concrete sign of prolonged neglect and disuse
key_terms.عَالِمٌ بَيْنَ جُهَّالٍ: A scholar among the ignorant — one whose knowledge is not sought or utilized
key_terms.مَسْجِدٌ خَرَابٌ: A ruined/desolate mosque — one that has fallen into disuse or neglect
key_terms.مُصْحَفٌ مُعَلَّقٌ: A hanging mushaf — a Quran copy left ornamentally without being read
key_terms.يَشْكُونَ: They complain/lament — an anthropomorphic expression for these objects presenting grievances before God

ai.seo_question: What three things complain to God in this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies three neglected religious institutions that, in a poetic anthropomorphic expression, complain before God: an abandoned mosque, an isolated scholar surrounded by the ignorant, and an unread Quran. The hadith calls Muslims to fulfil their duties toward sacred spaces, knowledge, and the Quran, reflecting the early Islamic concern for the vitality of communal worship and learning. The image of a neglected mushaf with dust on it was especially powerful for a community that regarded the physical Quran as a vessel of divine speech deserving constant engagement.
